title: Production Deployment Shows 404 Despite a Successful (Ready) Build
content:
When a customer reports a Ready deployment returning 404 in production, the first thing to clarify is that a Ready status only confirms the build completed — it does not confirm the routing layer resolved correctly. Requests are matched against routing metadata generated at build time (Framework Preset, Output Directory, rewrites/redirects), not a live filesystem scan, so a 404 can appear even though every file compiled cleanly.

Triage in this order:
1. Compare the auto-generated deployment URL against the custom domain. If only the custom domain 404s, this is a DNS/alias problem, not a build problem.
2. Open the deployment's Output tab and confirm the expected pages or serverless functions are actually present. An empty or unexpected output usually traces back to a wrong Output Directory or Root Directory setting — common after monorepo restructuring or a Framework Preset that reset to Other.
3. Check Runtime Logs filtered to 404 responses. No function invocation at all points to a routing/rewrite gap rather than a code failure.

For fastest recovery, don't wait to finish root-causing: use Instant Rollback to restore the last known-good deployment immediately. This preserves current environment variables and disables auto-promotion until explicitly undone, so fix the underlying setting on a preview deployment before re-promoting.
